visualDirections.name: Spatial field
visualDirections.principle: Give the subject a physical or system-like presence and let context orbit the object. Focal: subject.
visualDirections.geometry: One dominant field, deliberate asymmetry, native vectors/lines for relationships, large negative space.
visualDirections.surface: Mostly open canvas with one or two grounded surfaces; avoid enclosing every object.
visualDirections.density: Low-to-medium; density is concentrated around the focal object.
visualDirections.trade: Most distinctive and memorable, but requires stronger spatial placement and relationship design.

visualDirections.name: Editorial focus
visualDirections.principle: Treat the subject as an editorial hero with a small amount of high-value evidence. Focal: subject.
visualDirections.geometry: Oversized focal region with offset supporting context; no equal-width panel grid.
visualDirections.surface: Quiet canvas, restrained surfaces, typography doing more hierarchy work than borders.
visualDirections.density: Low; supporting information is compressed into a few intentional clusters.
visualDirections.trade: Calmest and most premium, but sacrifices raw information density.

visualDirections.name: Technical instrument
visualDirections.principle: Treat the subject as a live technical object with diagnostic layers and state evidence. Focal: subject.
visualDirections.geometry: Continuous primary surface, aligned readouts, rails and traces; use grids only where measurement benefits.
visualDirections.surface: Layered canvas/surface hierarchy with technical dividers and restrained state accents.
visualDirections.density: Medium-to-high, but structured into continuous fields instead of card stacks.
visualDirections.trade: Best for operators and developers; visually richer, but easier to over-densify.

passes.name: composition
add: Empty frames for: nav, subject, context
The primary visual as a single placeholder
hold: No text content beyond the headline
No repeated components - not one card, pill or row
No metrics. Pass 1 is where three-card layouts appear, and they are impossible to remove once every region is full.
passes.done: You can name each region and say why it exists, and the composition is one you would defend.

passes.name: information
add: Labels and content inside: nav, subject, context
Real data from: devices, topology links, per-link latency, memory pressure, GPU utilization, throughput, model placement, shard assignment, fit state
Controls the decision needs, and nothing more
Component instances via find_component, not rebuilt from rectangles
hold: No visual polish. Spacing and type tuning is pass 3, and doing it now means doing it twice.
passes.done: A person who knows the domain can read every value and complete the decision.

passes.name: visual refinement
add: Typography hierarchy and a monospaced face for machine data
Whitespace as deliberate space, not leftover
hold: No new content or regions. This pass only tunes what exists; adding here hides a structural problem.
passes.done: review_design returns no high-confidence findings and nothing looks accidental.

passes.name: interaction states
hold: No layout changes. A state that does not fit reveals a pass 1 or 2 problem, not a state problem.
passes.done: Every state that can occur is drawn, especially empty and error.

passes.name: QA
hold: No fixes invented from a render alone. Judge hierarchy and balance from the image; take structure from the tools.
passes.done: design_guard returns no FAIL, review_design has no high-confidence findings, and one render confirms the composition reads.

projectMemory:
Project design memory (durable notes about how this project should look):
- [project] Prefer topology as the hero visualization on system screens.
- [project] Prefer open surfaces over bordered cards; avoid unnecessary card borders.
- [project] Use accent colour sparingly: one action yellow, one health green, nothing neon.
- [project] Metrics are quiet instrument readouts, never a KPI wall.
- [project] Set identifiers, latencies and addresses in a monospaced face.
